notes.meaning: Moses looks ahead to a time when Israel will have lived through both God's blessings and His punishments. Even after being driven away into foreign lands because of their sins, they would still have hope. If they stopped to think about what happened and remembered God's words, the door to mercy would open. Remembering God's warnings is often the very first step in turning back to Him.

Moses describes what true repentance looks like. It is not just feeling sad about hardship, but returning to the Lord with all one's heart and soul. Parents and their children must listen closely to God's voice and begin obeying His commands again. Sincere faith always shows itself in a changed life.

God promises that if His people turn back to Him, He will feel deep pity for them. He will rescue them from their captivity and gather them together from every place where they were scattered. The Lord never forgets His hurting people when they seek His mercy.

Even if God's people are scattered to the farthest edges of the earth, distance is no problem for Him. The Lord has the power to reach them anywhere and bring them home. His reach is always greater than any trouble His people face.

The Lord promises to bring His people back into the land their ancestors once possessed. He will bless them so that they prosper and grow in number even more than their forefathers did. God's goodness to those who return is greater than their past suffering.

God promises to do an inward work that people cannot do on their own, which Moses calls circumcising the heart. This means God will clean away their love for sin and give them a genuine desire to love Him with all their heart and soul. When God gives a new heart, His people receive true spiritual life.

differ.view: Heart circumcision is the inward regenerating work of God's grace, promising the new covenant to all God's chosen people.

notes.meaning: When God restores His people, He will lift the curses from them and place those curses on their enemies. The nations that hated and mistreated them will face God's justice for their cruelty. God defends His children against those who try to crush them.

Once their hearts are renewed, the people will gladly listen to the Lord and follow all His commands. Their obedience will not be forced or bitter, but willing and faithful. Real forgiveness creates a thankful heart that wants to please God.

God promises to make His people prosper in their work, their families, their herds, and their crops. He will take great delight in doing them good, just as He rejoiced over their faithful ancestors. These blessings belong to those who listen to God and keep His laws with all their heart and soul. God delights to pour out kindness on those who walk closely with Him.

Moses tells the people that God's command is not too mysterious to understand or too hard to reach. God did not hide His will as a riddle that only a few scholars could solve. His words are stated clearly so that everyday people can grasp them and put them into practice.

No one needs to climb up to heaven or sail across distant seas on a dangerous quest to find God's truth. Ancient thinkers often traveled to far lands to search for wisdom, but God brought His message directly to Israel. God has made His will easily known without any impossible search.

God's message is close at hand, spoken on their lips in everyday words and understood in their minds so they can obey it. The Apostle Paul later explained that this closeness points to the message of faith in Christ, which a person believes in the heart and confesses with the mouth. God brings His saving truth right where we are.

Moses places a clear choice before the nation between life and good on one side, and death and evil on the other. God does not leave them guessing about what leads to joy or what leads to sorrow. Everyone naturally desires life, and God clearly marks the path that leads there.

The path to life is to love the Lord, walk in His ways, and keep His commands. Doing this brings health, growth, and God's blessing in the land they are entering. Genuine love for God always leads to joyful obedience.

Moses gives a serious warning about turning the heart away from God to worship false idols. Leaving the true God breaks their covenant, which was their sacred agreement with Him, and leads to certain ruin. Turning away from the Lord always brings deep loss.

Moses calls heaven and earth as lasting witnesses to this choice between life and death, blessing and curse. He warmly urges the people to choose life so that both they and their children may live. God clearly shows the consequences of our choices and urges us to choose what brings life.

differ.view: Fallen human beings cannot choose life by their own natural power, but God's Spirit graciously enables the elect to obey Him.

notes.meaning: Choosing life means loving the Lord, listening to His voice, and holding closely to Him every day. The Lord Himself is their life and the giver of their days, keeping the ancient promise He made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Walking closely with God is the source of all true peace and security.
